method: RTKLIB SPP (rnx2rtkp -p 0 -y 2): real pseudorange residuals + real satellite geometry.  Obstruction windows of 10/30/60/120/240 min every 3 h, 3 satellites kept (highest-elevation for the gap-length sweep; a multi-strategy sweep at 60 min also tests random and lowest-elevation obstruction).  A secondary sweep with 5 satellites (moderate obstruction, overdetermined) is also reported.  Clock anchored from the last full-sky epoch, then propagated during the gap three ways -- HOLD (frozen), LINRATE (pre-gap linear rate), KERNEL (anchor + the cross-day network kernel's band-limited deviation).  Each method's clock prior is weighted by its own empirical prediction error (two-pass: first compute each method's clock error, then use it as the prior sigma), so the comparison is fair.  Only epochs where ALL three methods produce a valid solution are kept (prevents SVD-rejection bias).  Kernel hyperparameters selected on a chronologically different training day (cross-day, leakage-free).  Actual 3-D position error vs the IGS SINEX daily solution (mm-level external truth, independent of the broadcast SPP test data).
truth_source: IGS SINEX daily solution (mm-level, independent of test data)

headline: Real RTKLIB SPP, 203 held-out station-days, 60-min 3-satellite obstruction windows: propagating the anchored clock with the network kernel cuts median 3-D position error from 21.9 m (hold constant) / 29.6 m (linear extrapolation) to 21.2 m -- +1% vs hold (95% CI [-1, +3]).
